newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity cut Bre-X stake just before stock collapsed.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity cut Bre-X stake just before stock collapsed.

text.p: Several Fidelity Investments mutual funds cut their holdings in the controversial Canadian gold mining company, Bre-X Minerals Ltd. in February, just weeks before the firm's stock crumbled.

According to Fidelity's monthly mutual fund guide, which was released Wednesday, the $135 million Fidelity Canada Fund cut its holdings in Bre-X parent Bresea Resources Ltd. from its top 10 stock holdings in February.

Fidelity's $320 million American Gold Fund and its $242 million Precious Metals & Minerals Fund also cut Bre-X from their top 10 holdings in February, the most recent date for the fund's activity, after being among their favourite shares in January.
Bre-X has estimated the Indonesian deposit contains 70.95 million ounces of gold, potentially the biggest in the world.

But the stock of Bre-X and its associated companies dived in late March after the company reported that deposits in its Busang gold mine, billed as the largest find this century, would fall far short of expectations.
Fidelity was one of the largest institutional holders of Bre-X, but the mutual fund company apparently cut a large part of its holdings in February.
Fidelity held 7.62 percent, or 50 million shares, of Bre-X at the end of 1996, Fidelity spokeswoman Robyn Tice said.
"Our holdings are sigificantly less, a fraction of what they were at the end of the year," she said.

Fifteen Fidelity funds, including Contrafund, Growth Company and Overseas, had a stake in Bre-X or its associated companies at the end of March. But only five of Fidelity's mutual funds were affected by losses of more than 0.5 percent at the end of March, she said.
